artworks.title: Leda and the Swan (detail: the personifications of Eurotas and Sparta), mosaic from the House of Aion
artworks.description: In this richly coloured floor mosaic from the House of Aion at Nea Paphos in Cyprus, the Spartan river Eurotas appears not as a mere landscape but in fully human form. The panel stages the myth of Leda, queen of Sparta, who is about to bathe in the Eurotas when Zeus, transformed into a swan, approaches her; flanking the scene stand the personifications of the river-god Eurotas himself and of Lakedaimonia (Sparta), the land and city named for his daughter. The detail shown here isolates Eurotas beside his offspring Sparta, a Late Antique pagan composition (c. 350 AD) that gives the eponymous founder of Laconia a rare individual likeness.

artworks.title: Statue of Eurotas, Leonidas Monument at Thermopylae
artworks.artist: Unknown (modern monument; photograph by Vaggelis Vlahos)
artworks.description: Part of the modern commemorative monument to Leonidas I at Thermopylae, this sculpture personifies Eurotas, the pre-Dorian king of Laconia who, according to Pausanias, drained the marsh-water of the plain by cutting a channel to the sea and gave his name to the river that remained. Set among the heroic figures honouring Sparta, the statue casts the mythic ancestor of the Spartan land as a foundational presence behind the city that later defended the pass, linking the legendary founder of the Eurotas valley to the historical Spartans who fought there.

artworks.title: Personification of the River Eurotas (Salamis thermae)
artworks.description: Floor mosaic from the Roman baths at Salamis on Cyprus: the river-god Eurotas reclines beside the wings of a swan in the southern sudatorium. The swan links the personification to Leda's myth on the Spartan stream, while the bath context treats Eurotas as a cooling water-power — the same Laconian river that Late Antique floors elsewhere name beside Sparta herself.

artworks.title: Eurotas and Lacedaemon mosaic
artworks.description: Late Antique mosaic in the Hatay Archaeology Museum, Antakya (inv. 826): facing personifications labelled as Eurotas and Lacedaemon (Lakedaimonia), the river-king and the land named for his line. Even far from Laconia, the pair travels as an emblem of Sparta's mythic geography — Eurotas as river and ancestor beside the personified Spartan plain.
